text:
Elaine: Quick sync — Lyra (prospective enterprise) wants a 2-week bakeoff. They plan to test three variants: base-1.3B, q4_1.3B, and a 'kv-optimized' build that uses prefix caching. Need: model catalog fit, infra compatibility (kv cache + quantization), and any enterprise blockers (KMS / HIPAA / residency). Can SE/ML/Security triage?

Raj: Yep. First questions: whats the max sequence length they’ll use, expected QPS per user, and model artifact format (HF / ONNX / ggml?). Also need the exact model files to run a quick compatibility scan (KV cache layout matters).

Elaine: They said seq len ~2048 for generative scoring, peak concurrent users ~50, QPS ~200 overall. Model artifacts: HF link + temp S3: https://huggingface.co/lyra/lyra-1.3b and s3://lyra-poc/artifacts/lyra_kv_opt.tar.gz (we have access).

Raj: Good. I can run `redwood model inspect` locally to check KV cache & kernel support. Example: 
```
redwood model inspect s3://lyra-poc/artifacts/lyra_kv_opt.tar.gz --show-quantization --show-kv-layout
```
If the kv layout matches our expected contiguous key/value blocks we're fine. If not, we'll need a conversion step (adds ~1 day).

Chris: On infra: for 1.3B variants we can run hosted inference but latency SLO at 2048+ with caching might push cost up. q4 reduces memory but we need the quantization recipe. For dedicated staging: 1x A10 + burst autoscaling should cover the bakeoff. Need expected token throughput to size autoscaler. Also: prefix/KV caching requires sticky routing; we should test with our sandbox network. I can provision a staging pool if legal signs the NDA.

Anna: Security flagging: Lyra is in healthcare space and asked about HIPAA. We only support HIPAA on Private deployments with BAAs. If they need HIPAA for the bakeoff, we must push them to Private or VIP contract. Also require KMS for key separation — do they have their own KMS? If yes, we can integrate. Please have them complete the short security questionnaire: https://redwood.internal/sec/questionnaire (answers will determine scope).

Jorge: Quick pricing ask from customer: ballpark monthly delta between hosted burst vs a 3-month dedicated reserved pool for the bakeoff. Elaine / Chris, can we get a rough number to share asap? They need to justify spend to procurement today.

Chris: Ballpark: hosted burst at expected QPS/token profile ~ $12k/mo (uncommitted, variable). Dedicated 3-month commit (1x A10 pool) roughly $7k/mo equivalent + initial setup/ingress egress assumptions. I’ll confirm with finance but that’s the thumb rule.

Raj: Next steps from ML side: I’ll run the `inspect` and a fast compatibility run in our staging pool. If conversion needed I estimate +1 business day. Will ping with scan output and `redwood catalog add --variant` suggestion.

Elaine: Thanks — action items: Raj runs catalog/kv check (ETA 6h), Chris to confirm pricing + staging slot (ETA EOD), Anna to confirm HIPAA/KMS constraints (ETA EOD). Jorge will loop in customer procurement with the ballpark. If anyone needs the S3 creds again DM me. :thumbsup:

InfraBot: Staging pool request queued: ticket INF-4219. ETA for pool spin-up (post-approval): 4h.

Raj: Scan results — quick note (will post full): base + q4 are fine; kv-optimized uses a nonstandard split-by-token layout, conversion script required. I'll attach the minimal conversion patch in the scan report.

Anna: Noted — if conversion touches token-level metadata we need to review for PII stripping in the pipeline. Keep me looped.

Elaine: Perfect. I'll update the customer with this plan and ask them to sign NDA + complete questionnaire. We'll reconvene once Raj's report is in.

Chris: I'll drop estimated committed quote in this thread once finance confirms.

Jorge: Thx all — I’ll schedule a 15m sync tomorrow after Raj posts results.
